raw_case_text:
Patient information: a 6-year-old male presented to the Emergency Department of the University Hospital, Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Kumasi, Ghana with two days' history of epigastric pain, chest pains, fever, and vomiting. The mother had administered paracetamol syrup prior to reporting to the hospital, but symptoms did not resolve. He had no known chronic illness and no previous history of hospital admission.
Clinical results: on examination, the patient looked restless, pale, and anicteric with a temperature of 36.8 C. Vital signs were unremarkable. The liver was palpable, 2 cm below the right subcostal margin, smooth surface, and mildly tender. The patient had low haemoglobin, elevated white blood cell (WBC), low platelets, elevated liver enzymes, and deranged renal function. Hepatitis B (HBsAg) and C (HCV Ab) were non-reactive (Table 1).
Diagnostic approach and therapeutic intervention: on the first day, the patient was given intravenous (IV) artesunate 3.0 mg/kg body weight (55 mg) at 0, 12, and 24 hours, IV paracetamol 275 mg three times daily, and other supportive therapy. He was also transfused 366 mL of whole blood.
On the second day of admission, the patient started experiencing fever (temperature of 40.1 C) with chills and rigors, altered level of consciousness (Blantyre coma score of 4/5), and breathing difficulty (respiratory rate 30 cycles per minute). On chest examination, air entry was adequate bilaterally with vesicular breath sounds. His oxygen saturation was 99% on intranasal oxygen at 6 liters per minute. Due to these clinical features, a nasopharyngeal sample was taken for COVID-19. Post-transfusion laboratory investigations on day 3 showed an improvement in the haemoglobin level as well as the liver enzymes (Table 1). Routine urine analysis showed leucocytes - trace, blood +, and protein +.
On admission day 5, he was started on suspension cefpodoxime 100mg bd for 5 days and other treatments continued. Laboratory results retrieved showed no malaria parasites and full blood count showed approximately 1g/dl drop in haemoglobin level and normalization of the platelets. The patient s temperature (36.5 C), respiratory rate (18 cycles per minute) and level of consciousness (Blantyre coma scale 5/5) progressively improved and were normal.
Follow-up: the patient was discharged from the ward to self-isolate at home, awaiting the RT-PCR results which were reported positive for COVID-19. Clinical results and diagnostic approach are summarized in Table 1.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 6-year-old male presented to the emergency department with a 2-day history of epigastric pain, chest pain, fever, and vomiting.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed epigastric pain, chest pain, fever, and vomiting 2 days prior to admission in Kumasi, Ghana. His mother administered paracetamol syrup at home without symptom resolution.
subjective.past_medical_history: No known chronic illness and no previous history of hospital admission.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for epigastric pain, chest pain, fever, and vomiting; prior home use of paracetamol syrup.

objective.physical_examination: On admission, restless, pale, and anicteric with temperature 36.8 C and otherwise unremarkable vital signs; abdomen showed a smooth, mildly tender palpable liver 2 cm below the right subcostal margin. On hospital day 2, developed fever (40.1 C) with chills and rigors, altered consciousness (Blantyre coma score 4/5), tachypnea (30 cpm), adequate bilateral air entry with vesicular breath sounds, and SpO2 99% on intranasal oxygen at 6 L/min.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission labs showed low hemoglobin, elevated WBC, low platelets, elevated liver enzymes, deranged renal function, and non-reactive HBsAg and HCV Ab. Day 3 post-transfusion labs showed improved hemoglobin and liver enzymes; routine urinalysis showed trace leukocytes, blood (+), and protein (+). Day 5 labs showed an ~1 g/dL drop in hemoglobin and normalized platelets.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Clinical malaria complicated by severe anemia and SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) co-infection. Treated on day 1 with IV artesunate 3.0 mg/kg (55 mg) at 0, 12, and 24 hours, IV paracetamol 275 mg TID, supportive care, and transfusion of 366 mL whole blood; started oral cefpodoxime suspension 100 mg BID for 5 days on day 5. Blood smear on day 5 was negative for malaria parasites, while nasopharyngeal RT-PCR returned positive for COVID-19. Temperature (36.5 C), respiratory rate (18 cpm), and consciousness (Blantyre coma score 5/5) normalized, and he was discharged home to self-isolate.
